model.name: Alias / Same-as Mapping
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-036 is a composable mixin that lets any subject model carry, qualify and govern assertions that two or more identifiers or records held by different authorities designate the same referent, or explicitly do not. It covers the assertion itself (participants, direction, equivalence strength), the qualification of the assertion (asserting authority, confidence or assurance level, supporting evidence, context and temporal validity), explicit not-same constraints, the assertion lifecycle (proposed, asserted, disputed, superseded, retracted), the derived cluster or endpoint views that follow from an assertion set, and the reporting surface over all of the above: conflict reports, change-impact reports, disposition-readiness reports and the notification content that describes alias change to downstream consumers. The model is storage- and interface-neutral: JSON, YAML, Markdown, RDF, Git, MCP and MongoDB are projections of these semantics, not the semantics. The model states facts and findings; it never adjudicates a contested equivalence, never executes deletion or retention, never enforces policy, never constructs an audit trail and never delivers a notification.
in_scope: Directed and symmetric equivalence assertions (same-as, alias-of, replaced-by, see-also) between two or more identifier endpoints or records held by different authorities.

Qualification of each assertion by equivalence strength (strict logical identity, exact match, close match, referential alias), asserting authority, confidence or assurance level, and supporting evidence.
Context scoping and temporal scoping of equivalence, including a validity interval for the equivalence claim and the separate observation time at which the claim was recorded.
Explicit not-same (difference) constraints and the way they interact logically with equivalence claims over the same endpoint pair.
Assertion lifecycle states and transitions: proposed, asserted, disputed, superseded, retracted and withdrawn by the asserting authority.
Derived cluster or endpoint views computed from an assertion set, including the merge and split of those derived views.
Conflict reporting, change-impact reporting and disposition-readiness reporting over the assertion set and its derived views, with declared coverage and residual uncertainty.
Notification content that describes an alias change for downstream consumers, expressed independently of any delivery channel.
out_of_scope: Minting, syntax, checksum rules and governance of the identifiers being aliased; those belong to the parent identification model.
Computation of probabilistic match scores or blocking keys by an entity-resolution or record-linkage engine.
Execution of deletion, destruction, transfer, anonymisation or retention schedules, and the legal authority that permits them.
Placement, release, scope and legal effect of legal holds, litigation holds and records freezes.
Subscription management, notification delivery, receipt acknowledgement, retry and escalation.
Construction, sealing and retention of tamper-evident audit trails.
Authorization decisions and runtime policy evaluation or enforcement.
Merge and unmerge execution inside a source system of record, including rewriting that system's own primary keys.

boundary_notes.distinction: The parent model owns identifier issuance, scheme registration, syntax and resolution. WM-XCT-036 only references identifier endpoints and states equivalence or non-equivalence between them; a report cites an endpoint, it never re-mints or re-formats one. Because OWL 2 makes no unique name assumption, two distinct identifiers are neither same nor different by default, so equivalence must be asserted by this model rather than inferred from the identifier model.

PROV owns Activity, Agent, Generation, Derivation and Invalidation record semantics. WM-XCT-036 attaches provenance to its own report instances and to impacted items using those terms as an alignment; it does not define what an activity or agent is, and its report instances are not a general provenance store.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Records retention, disposition authority and legal hold register model
boundary_notes.distinction: That model owns retention schedules, disposition authority, hold and freeze placement and release, and the execution of destruction or transfer. WM-XCT-036 reports readiness only: it classifies a record as eligible, blocked, retained as residue or externally governed, cites the governing rule and hold by reference, and hands off. Suspension and resumption of disposition are decided and effected by the records authority, not here.

Linked Data Notifications separates the sender, receiver and consumer roles from the payload, and deliberately leaves the payload vocabulary open. WM-XCT-036 produces payload content describing an alias change; inbox discovery, POST delivery, storage, receipt and escalation belong entirely to the notification service.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Shape or constraint validation service and policy evaluation engine
boundary_notes.distinction: A SHACL-style engine executes constraint evaluation and emits a validation report. WM-XCT-036 aligns the shape of its conflict report to that pattern (focus item, source constraint, severity, message) so that consumers can read it uniformly, but referencing the report structure grants no ownership of evaluation, execution or enforcement; the engine and its runtime remain external.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Data quality and confidence measurement model
boundary_notes.distinction: Metric definition and metric computation belong to the quality model. WM-XCT-036 cites externally computed measurements and externally assigned assurance levels when reporting a confidence-divergence conflict, and never recomputes or normalises them into a single scale.

Report issuance, reissue and release are events that the adopting Dimension's audit model may record. A WM-XCT-036 report instance is an evidentiary output with provenance, not an audit record; it carries no tamper-evidence guarantee and confers no audit-trail semantics.

sources.title: Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.relevance: Section 3.6 defines a validation report as a set of results carrying sh:focusNode, sh:resultPath, sh:value, sh:sourceShape, sh:sourceConstraintComponent, sh:detail, sh:resultMessage and exactly one sh:resultSeverity from sh:Violation, sh:Warning or sh:Info. This is the normative pattern for a report that states findings without resolving them, and sh:conforms shows how a report distinguishes 'no results' from 'validated as correct'.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Supplies the lineage vocabulary used by impact and report-instance provenance: prov:wasDerivedFrom, prov:wasRevisionOf, prov:wasInvalidatedBy with prov:invalidatedAtTime, prov:generatedAtTime, prov:qualifiedDerivation, prov:wasAttributedTo and prov:Bundle. prov:alternateOf and prov:specializationOf give a weaker, non-identity alternative to strict same-as that conflict reports must be able to distinguish.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Section 10 defines the graded mapping vocabulary skos:mappingRelation, exactMatch, closeMatch, broadMatch, narrowMatch and relatedMatch. exactMatch is declared an owl:TransitiveProperty while closeMatch is deliberately not transitive 'to avoid the possibility of compound errors when combining mappings across more than two concept schemes' - the direct normative basis for reporting equivalence-strength conflicts and chain-composition risk.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Structural Specification and Functional-Style Syntax (Second Edition)
sources.relevance: Section 9.6 defines SameIndividual (individuals are the same) and DifferentIndividuals (individuals are not identical). Asserting both over the same pair renders the ontology inconsistent, which is the formal basis for the not-same violation conflict class. OWL 2 makes no unique name assumption, so absence of a conflict is not evidence of sameness.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Release 5 - Patient Resource
sources.relevance: Patient.link with the LinkType value set (replaced-by, replaces, refer, seealso) is a deployed normative model of directed supersession and non-replacing reference between duplicate records of the same real-world subject; Patient.link is a modifier element, showing that link type changes the interpretation of the record. Patient.active supports lifecycle-state reporting.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Release 5 - Person Resource
sources.relevance: Person.link.assurance and the IdentityAssuranceLevel value set (level1 probabilistic, level2 moderate, level3 e.g. government photo identification, level4 highest) provide a normative ordinal confidence scale attached to a cross-system identity link, and the basis for reporting confidence divergence between authorities.

sources.title: HL7 FHIR Release 5 - OperationOutcome Resource
sources.relevance: A collection of error, warning or information messages resulting from a system action, with issue.severity (fatal, error, warning, information, success), issue.code, issue.details, issue.diagnostics and issue.expression. It is explicitly not a clinical decision or adjudication, which is the second independent precedent for a report that carries graded findings without deciding them.

sources.title: Universal Electronic Records Management (ERM) Requirements
sources.organization: National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), United States
sources.relevance: Organises electronic records requirements into Capture, Maintenance and Use, Disposal, Transfer, Metadata and Reporting phases, with Must Have and Should Have gradings. Establishes that disposal, transfer, metadata and reporting are distinct governed capabilities, and that reporting is a first-class requirement area separate from execution of disposal.

sources.title: Federal Records Centers Program - Freeze Process Overview (FAQ)
sources.organization: National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), United States
sources.version_or_date: Page last reviewed 29 January 2024; cites 36 CFR 1228.54 and 44 U.S.C. 2909
sources.relevance: Distinguishes a freeze (requested of NARA for records in Federal Records Center custody) from a litigation hold or moratorium issued by an agency Counsel's Office, states that a hold suspends the normal disposition cycle to prevent premature disposal, and that normal disposition resumes only on formal notification. Primary evidence that hold placement and release are owned by an external authority, not by the reporting system.

sources.title: Linked Data Notifications
sources.relevance: Separates sender, receiver and consumer roles from the notification payload and states that 'the actual vocabulary of the payload is deliberately not specified here'. Inbox discovery uses an HTTP Link header with rel http://www.w3.org/ns/ldp#inbox. Normative basis for producing notification content while leaving subscription, delivery and receipt to an external service.

sources.title: Activity Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Defines Update, Delete and Undo activity content and the Tombstone object with formerType (the type of the object that was deleted) and deleted (a timestamp for when the object was deleted). Supplies a standards-based shape for change-notice content and for the tombstone residue that survives an authorised disposition.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (General Data Protection Regulation), Article 19 - Notification obligation regarding rectification or erasure of personal data or restriction of processing
sources.organization: The National Archives (United Kingdom), legislation.gov.uk rendering of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016
sources.version_or_date: Regulation of 27 April 2016; legislation.gov.uk assimilated-law rendering
sources.relevance: The controller must communicate any rectification, erasure or restriction of processing to each recipient to whom the personal data have been disclosed, 'unless this proves impossible or involves disproportionate effort', and must inform the data subject about those recipients on request. Directly grounds downstream-reference impact reporting, the reach-completeness qualifier and the notification-content obligation.

sources.title: Data on the Web Best Practices: Data Quality Vocabulary (DQV)
sources.relevance: dqv:QualityMeasurement, dqv:Metric, dqv:Dimension, dqv:QualityAnnotation and dqv:UserQualityFeedback, with dqv:isMeasurementOf and dqv:value, and integration with PROV-O and Web Annotation. Supplies the referenced (not owned) vocabulary for citing externally computed confidence and completeness measures inside a report. Publication as a Working Group Note does not imply W3C endorsement, so alignment is non-normative.

sources.title: RFC 3339 - Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Requires a two-digit time-second and a mandatory time offset of 'Z' or a signed hour:minute offset; '-00:00' means UTC is known but the local offset is not, which 'differs semantically from an offset of Z or +00:00'. Governs every time value in this model and lets event, observation and ingestion times be compared without ambiguity.

bundles.name: Conflict and Change-Impact Reporting
bundles.description: Everything needed to state, without deciding, what is incompatible within a federated alias assertion set, and what a change to that set does to assertions, derived cluster views and downstream references.
bundles.rationale: Two independent normative precedents establish the shape of a report that grades findings but does not resolve them: the SHACL validation report (results with focus item, source constraint and severity) and the FHIR OperationOutcome (severity-graded issues that are explicitly not an adjudication). The substance of what can conflict is fixed by OWL 2 (SameIndividual versus DifferentIndividuals is an inconsistency; no unique name assumption), SKOS (exactMatch is transitive, closeMatch deliberately is not, to avoid compound errors), FHIR link types and assurance levels (directed supersession, ordinal confidence), and PROV-O (derivation, revision and invalidation lineage). Grouping conflict and impact together is justified because both are read-only projections over the same assertion set at a declared observation time, and both must publish their own coverage limits rather than imply completeness.

layers.name: Conflict Surface and Report Request Contract
layers.description: What can be in conflict within an alias assertion set, and the bounded, reproducible request contract under which a conflict report is produced.

findings.name: Conflict class taxonomy over alias assertions
findings.description: The governed set of conflict classes a report may state over an alias assertion set: incompatible asserting authorities over the same endpoint pair; incompatible equivalence strength or semantics; divergent confidence or assurance; mismatched context of assertion; temporal incompatibility between validity intervals; conflicting or absent evidence; violation of an explicit not-same constraint; and incompatible lifecycle states. Each class is defined by what makes two claims incompatible rather than merely different, and by the comparison that detects it. The taxonomy is extensible by an adopting Dimension through namespaced codes but the base classes are fixed so that consumers can rely on them.

questions.text: Which conflict classes may a conflict report state over an alias assertion set, and how is each class defined?
answer_data: Conflict class code from the governed base vocabulary
Normative definition of incompatibility for that class
Comparison operation that detects the class
Minimum number and role of participating assertions

questions.text: How does a report distinguish a formal not-same violation from a mere disagreement about equivalence strength?
answer_data: Flag indicating whether the incompatibility is logically entailed (SameIndividual plus DifferentIndividuals) or semantic (exactMatch versus closeMatch versus alternateOf)
Reference to the asserted difference constraint
Reference to the strength vocabulary and version each participant used

questions.text: What makes two competing assertions genuinely conflicting rather than merely scoped to different contexts?
answer_data: Context qualifier of each participating assertion
Result of context-overlap test
Reason code for classifying as conflict, as scoped-difference, or as undecidable

questions.text: Which conflict classes become detectable only when validity intervals or observation times are compared?
answer_data: Validity interval start and end of each participant
Observation time of each participant
Interval relation code (overlap, meets, disjoint, unbounded)
Flag for conflicts that vanish when intervals are respected

questions.text: How may an adopting Dimension extend the conflict class vocabulary without breaking existing report consumers?
answer_data: Extension namespace identifier
Vocabulary version bound to the report
Consumer rule for unknown codes
Deprecation state of any base code

data_elements.name: Conflict class code
data_elements.description: Governed code identifying the class of incompatibility being stated, drawn from the base vocabulary or a declared extension namespace.

data_elements.name: Conflict class definition
data_elements.description: Normative text stating what makes participating claims incompatible for this class, so that a consumer can falsify the classification.

data_elements.name: Detection basis
data_elements.description: The comparison that produced the classification, for example logical entailment over difference axioms, strength-vocabulary comparison, interval relation, or assurance-level divergence.

data_elements.name: Equivalence strength vocabulary binding
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the vocabulary each participating assertion used to express equivalence strength, required because transitive and deliberately non-transitive relations must not be silently merged.

data_elements.name: Conflict class extension namespace
data_elements.description: Namespace under which an adopting Dimension registers additional conflict classes.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The taxonomy is governed controlled-vocabulary content, not a produced document. It is consumed by reference from every conflict report instance through a vocabulary identifier and version, and materialising it as a separate artifact per report would create drifting copies of a definition that must stay single-sourced. The classes themselves are inline reference data owned by the vocabulary steward role.

findings.name: Conflict report request scope, preconditions and failure modes
findings.description: The bounded request contract that makes a conflict report reproducible and honest about its own limits: which assertion population is in scope, which preconditions must hold before a report can be produced, which failure mode applies when each precondition is unmet, how partial coverage is declared when a participating authority is unreachable, and which observation cut-off time governs the whole report.

questions.text: What scope selector defines the assertion population that a conflict report covers?
answer_data: Selector expression over endpoints, authorities, subject types or clusters
Included and explicitly excluded authority references
Resolved count of assertions in scope
Immutable scope binding reference

questions.text: Which preconditions must hold before a conflict report can be produced, and which failure mode applies when each is unmet?
answer_data: Precondition identifier and outcome
Failure mode code (unresolvable scope, snapshot unavailable, vocabulary version mismatch, authority unreachable)
Whether the failure aborts the report or degrades it
Failure outcome record reference

questions.text: How does a report record partial coverage when a participating authority is unreachable at production time?
answer_data: Unreachable authority reference and reason
Coverage completeness qualifier for the affected scope
Statement that absence of a conflict for that authority is not a negative finding
Retry or re-request guidance reference

questions.text: Which observation cut-off time governs the report, and how is it kept distinct from the event times of the assertions it covers?
answer_data: Observation cut-off timestamp with explicit offset
Covered event-time range of the assertion population
Input snapshot ingestion timestamp
Statement that assertions with a later event time are outside the report

data_elements.name: Scope selector
data_elements.description: Declarative expression resolving the assertion population in scope for a report, retained so a later run over the same snapshot yields the same population.

data_elements.name: Precondition outcome
data_elements.description: Per-precondition record of whether the condition held, was waived, or triggered a failure mode.

data_elements.name: Failure mode code
data_elements.description: Code identifying why report production aborted or degraded, aligned to a severity-graded issue vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Coverage completeness qualifier
data_elements.description: Explicit statement of how completely the declared scope was actually examined, cited as a referenced quality measurement where one exists.

data_elements.name: Observation cut-off time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit seconds and offset defining the instant beyond which no input was considered.

findings.inline_only_rationale: A report request is an input binding and a set of gate outcomes, not a retained document. Its durable value is carried forward into the released report instance as the frozen scope binding, snapshot reference and cut-off time, so persisting it as a second artifact would duplicate the reproducibility basis and create two things that can disagree about the same run.

layers.name: Conflict Statement Composition and Neutrality
layers.description: How an individual conflict is stated so that it is traceable, gradeable and independently checkable, and the rules that stop a report from quietly resolving what it is only supposed to expose.

findings.name: Individual conflict result record
findings.description: The atomic unit of a conflict report: a single stated incompatibility naming its participating assertions, the identifier endpoints and asserting authorities involved, the conflict class, an optional severity or significance grade, a human-readable message and the evidence and comparison basis that lets a consumer re-derive the finding. The record grades significance but decides nothing: it never marks a participant as correct, never removes a participant and never changes any assertion's lifecycle state.

questions.text: What identifies a single conflict result within a report, and is that identity stable when the report is reissued?
answer_data: Conflict result identifier
Derivation rule for the identifier (participants plus class plus context)
Stability guarantee across reissues of the same series
Link to the corresponding result in a prior instance

questions.text: Which participating assertions, asserting authorities and identifier endpoints must every conflict result cite?
answer_data: Participating assertion references
Asserting authority reference per participant
Identifier endpoint references
Role of each participant in the conflict (both required, or focus plus counterpart)

questions.text: What severity or significance grade may a conflict result carry, and what does that grade explicitly not decide?
answer_data: Severity code and the vocabulary it comes from
Explicit non-adjudication statement bound to the result
Named party or model responsible for any resolution decision
Statement that severity is not a truth ranking of participants

questions.text: What evidence and comparison basis must be cited so a consumer can independently re-derive the stated conflict?
answer_data: Evidence references per participant
Source constraint or rule reference that produced the result
Values or interval relations compared
Snapshot reference the comparison ran against

data_elements.name: Conflict result identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier for one stated conflict, derived deterministically from participants, class and context so that the same conflict keeps the same identity across reissues.

data_elements.name: Conflict participant
data_elements.description: Reference to one participating alias assertion together with its asserting authority and identifier endpoint, and its role in the conflict.

data_elements.name: Conflict severity grade
data_elements.description: Graded significance of the stated conflict drawn from a declared severity vocabulary; informational only, never a ruling on which participant is correct.

data_elements.name: Source constraint reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the rule, shape or definition whose comparison produced this result, so the finding is attributable rather than opaque.

data_elements.name: Conflict evidence reference
data_elements.description: References to the evidence each participant relies on, including any externally computed assurance level or quality measurement.

data_elements.name: Conflict result message
data_elements.description: Human-readable statement of the incompatibility, phrased descriptively and without recommending a winner.

artifacts.name: Alias conflict report instance
artifacts.description: A released, immutable report over a frozen assertion scope, containing a conformance-style summary, the ordered set of conflict result records, the declared coverage and completeness statement, the vocabulary version bindings and the report provenance. It states incompatibilities and adjudicates none.
media_or_form: Structured record set with a conformance summary and an ordered result collection
Graph serialisation aligned to a validation-report shape
Tabular or document rendering derived from the same canonical record set
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the report series identifier plus the instance identifier minted per artifact_rules.identity_priority; a conflict result inside the instance is identified by als-report-conflict-result-id, which is deterministic over participants, class and context so results can be diffed across instances.

findings.name: Non-adjudication and minority-claim preservation
findings.description: The rules that keep a conflict report honest: every participating claim that falls inside the declared scope appears in the report regardless of its authority weight or confidence, any ordering presented is labelled with its basis and marked as presentational rather than resolutive, exclusion by scope is disclosed and distinguished from exclusion by judgement, and the party or model accountable for any downstream adjudication is named by reference rather than acted for.

questions.text: Which rules prevent a conflict report from dropping, collapsing or down-weighting a minority or low-confidence claim out of view?
answer_data: Inclusion status per in-scope claim
Prohibition rule identifier that forbids silent omission
Count of in-scope claims versus count of reported claims
Reconciliation statement when the two counts differ

questions.text: How is an authority-weighted or confidence-weighted ordering presented so that it cannot be read as a resolution?
answer_data: Ordering basis descriptor and the property it sorts on
Presentational-only marker
Referenced measurement or assurance level used for ordering
Statement that ordering does not alter any assertion state

questions.text: How does a report disclose that a claim was excluded by scope rather than by judgement about its merit?
answer_data: Exclusion reason code (out of scope, unreachable authority, later than cut-off)
Selector clause that caused the exclusion
Excluded claim reference where the reference itself is in scope to disclose

questions.text: Who is recorded as accountable for the adjudication that the report deliberately leaves open?
answer_data: Referral target reference (role, model or adopting-Dimension body)
Statement that this model performs no resolution
Open-conflict handoff payload reference

data_elements.name: Claim inclusion status
data_elements.description: Per in-scope claim, whether it was included in the report, and if not, the disclosed reason.

data_elements.name: Exclusion reason
data_elements.description: Reason code and selector clause explaining a scope-based exclusion, so that omission is never mistaken for a merit judgement.

data_elements.name: Ordering basis descriptor
data_elements.description: Declared property and direction used to order results or participants, with an explicit presentational-only marker.

data_elements.name: Adjudication referral reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the role, model or body accountable for resolving an open conflict, recorded so the report can hand off without acting.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are invariants that constrain how the conflict report artifact is composed, plus per-claim inclusion metadata that lives inside that artifact. Emitting a separate neutrality document would produce a policy statement this model does not own and would let the rules drift from the reports they govern; the rules belong in the model's policy layer and their per-run evidence belongs inline in the report.

layers.name: Change Impact Projection
layers.description: Which changes to an alias assertion set trigger an impact report, and how impact is projected across assertions, derived cluster views and downstream references with full lineage and declared uncertainty.

findings.name: Impact trigger event classification
findings.description: The classified change events that warrant an impact report: supersession of an assertion by a later one; retraction or withdrawal of an assertion by its authority; merge of two endpoint clusters into one; split of a cluster into two or more; a policy change that alters which equivalence strengths or confidence levels are admissible; and discovery that a previously accepted strong-identity assertion was false. Retraction and supersession are kept apart because their retrospective reach differs: supersession leaves the prior claim historically true within its interval, retraction asserts it was never sound.

questions.text: Which change events trigger an impact report, and how is each event class defined?
answer_data: Trigger class code (supersession, retraction, merge, split, policy change, false strong identity)
Definition and minimum evidence for each class
Reference to the triggering change record
Event time of the trigger with explicit offset

questions.text: How is a retraction distinguished from a supersession in impact terms?
answer_data: Prior lifecycle state and posterior lifecycle state
Whether the prior claim remains historically valid within its interval
Invalidation time where the claim was invalidated rather than revised
Revision link where a successor assertion exists

questions.text: When a strong-identity assertion is later found false, what retrospective scope must the impact report cover?
answer_data: Retrospective window start (earliest event time at which the false claim could have propagated)
Set of derived views computed while the false claim held
Downstream references issued during the window
Statement of what could not be enumerated

questions.text: How is a policy change that alters admissible equivalence strength or confidence represented as an impact trigger?
answer_data: Policy reference and version before and after
Issuing authority reference
Effective time of the policy change
Set of assertions whose admissibility status changes, without any state change being applied

data_elements.name: Impact trigger class code
data_elements.description: Governed code for the class of change that occasioned the impact report.

data_elements.name: Trigger event time
data_elements.description: RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit seconds and offset for when the triggering change occurred, distinct from when this model observed it.

data_elements.name: Trigger source reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the change record, authority decision or policy version that constitutes the trigger, held by whichever model owns it.

data_elements.name: Retrospective window
data_elements.description: Bounded event-time interval during which a now-falsified or superseded claim could have propagated, defining the report's backward reach.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Trigger classification is governed vocabulary plus per-run parameters that are carried inside the impact report artifact. The triggering change records themselves are owned by the assertion lifecycle surface and by the policy or authority models that issued them, so materialising a separate trigger artifact here would duplicate records this model does not own.

findings.name: Impact surfaces, lineage and residual uncertainty
findings.description: Impact is projected across three surfaces with distinct units. At assertion level the unit is a single alias assertion whose admissibility, strength or lifecycle relevance changes. At cluster-view level the unit is a derived endpoint cluster that gains, loses, merges or splits members, and the fate of each member must be stated. At downstream-reference level the unit is a consuming reference that resolved through the changed alias. Every impacted item carries lineage back to the triggering change and to its prior state, and the report states the residual uncertainty where downstream reach cannot be fully enumerated rather than implying complete coverage.

questions.text: Which impact surfaces must an impact report cover, and what is the unit of impact on each?
answer_data: Surface code (assertion, cluster view, downstream reference)
Unit of impact and its identifier type per surface
Impacted item count per surface
Surfaces explicitly not assessed and why

questions.text: What lineage must be attached so a consumer can trace an impacted item back to the triggering change and to its prior state?
answer_data: Derivation chain from impacted item to trigger
Prior state reference or snapshot for the impacted item
Revision or invalidation link where applicable
Agent attributed with the triggering change

questions.text: How does the report represent a cluster that splits into two or more clusters, including the fate of every member?
answer_data: Predecessor cluster reference
Successor cluster references
Per-member assignment with the assertion that justifies it
Members whose assignment is undetermined and the reason

questions.text: How is residual uncertainty expressed when downstream reference reach cannot be fully enumerated?
answer_data: Reach completeness qualifier and the measurement it cites
Known-unknown categories (unindexed consumers, cached copies, offline replicas)
Effort basis for stopping enumeration
Explicit statement that unenumerated does not mean unaffected

questions.text: Which downstream references are knowable to this model, and which are knowable only to the consuming system?
answer_data: Downstream reference index reference and its owner
Index completeness declaration supplied by that owner
Consumer-side reconciliation guidance
Boundary statement that consumer-side propagation is not performed here

data_elements.name: Impact surface code
data_elements.description: Code identifying which of the assertion, cluster-view or downstream-reference surfaces an impacted item belongs to.

data_elements.name: Impacted item reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the assertion, derived cluster or downstream reference that the triggering change affects.

data_elements.name: Prior state reference
data_elements.description: Reference or snapshot capturing the impacted item as it stood immediately before the trigger, without which impact cannot be verified.

data_elements.name: Lineage chain
data_elements.description: Ordered derivation, revision and invalidation links connecting the impacted item to the triggering change and to the responsible agent.

data_elements.name: Cluster member fate
data_elements.description: Per-member outcome of a merge or split, naming the successor cluster and the assertion that justifies the assignment, or recording that the assignment is undetermined.

data_elements.name: Downstream reach completeness
data_elements.description: Declared completeness of downstream-reference enumeration, citing the index that supplied it and the effort basis for stopping.

data_elements.name: Residual uncertainty qualifier
data_elements.description: Structured statement of what remains unknown about impact, including known-unknown categories, so a consumer never reads silence as absence of effect.

artifacts.name: Alias change-impact report instance
artifacts.description: A released, immutable report describing a single classified triggering change and its projected effects across the assertion, cluster-view and downstream-reference surfaces, with per-item lineage back to the trigger and prior state, per-member fate for merges and splits, and an explicit reach-completeness and residual-uncertainty statement. It projects effects and performs none of them.
media_or_form: Structured record set partitioned by impact surface with an embedded lineage graph
Graph serialisation using derivation, revision and invalidation relations
Rendered summary derived from the same canonical record set
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the report series identifier plus the instance identifier minted per artifact_rules.identity_priority, and bound to exactly one trigger source reference and trigger event time; an impacted item entry is keyed by impact surface code plus impacted item reference.

bundles.name: Disposition Readiness and Report Release Governance
bundles.description: Reporting on whether alias mapping records are ready for disposition without performing it, and governing the report instances themselves as identified, provenance-bearing, access-scoped objects whose delivery is somebody else's job.
bundles.rationale: NARA's Universal ERM Requirements treat Disposal, Transfer, Metadata and Reporting as distinct requirement areas, which supports reporting readiness as a capability separate from executing disposal. NARA's freeze process documentation shows that holds and freezes are placed by an agency Counsel's Office or by NARA, suspend the normal disposition cycle, and are released only on formal notification from that authority - so a readiness report can cite a block but can neither create nor lift it. GDPR Article 19 obliges a controller to communicate rectification, erasure or restriction to each recipient unless that proves impossible or involves disproportionate effort, which is exactly a downstream notification-content obligation with an explicit effort limit. Linked Data Notifications separates payload from sender, receiver and consumer roles and leaves the payload vocabulary open, and the Activity Vocabulary supplies Update, Delete, Undo and the Tombstone object with formerType and deleted. PROV-O and RFC 3339 govern report-instance lineage and time.

layers.name: Disposition Readiness Assessment
layers.description: Classifying each alias mapping record's readiness for disposition, citing the governing rule and any blocking hold, declaring what must survive as residue, and handing execution to the authority that owns it.

findings.name: Disposition readiness status classification
findings.description: Every alias mapping record in scope receives exactly one readiness status: eligible (a cited retention rule has run and no block applies); blocked (a cited legal hold, litigation hold or records freeze suspends disposition until the issuing authority formally releases it); retained (the record must persist as a tombstone or provenance residue even after content disposal); externally governed (disposition authority sits with a source authority or jurisdiction outside the adopting Dimension); or not assessed (readiness could not be determined within the report's observation window). findings.name: Required residue and execution handoff

layers.name: Report Instance Identity, Provenance and Release Boundary
layers.description: Treating a released report as a governed object in its own right: how it is identified and versioned, which times it must carry, what provenance makes it reproducible, how it is access-scoped and redacted before release, and where this model's responsibility for change notification stops.

findings.name: Report instance identity, provenance, access scope and notification content
findings.description: A report instance is an immutable, identified, provenance-bearing object belonging to a named series. It carries its generation time, the observation cut-off, the covered event-time range and the input snapshot ingestion time as separate values; corrections are issued as new instances linked to their predecessor by a revision relation, never by editing a released instance. Provenance records the generating agent, the frozen scope binding and the input snapshot so the instance is reproducible. Each section carries an access scope and any redaction applied before release. Where a change must be communicated, this model composes notification content describing the change and pointing at the released instance; discovery of an inbox, delivery, storage, receipt acknowledgement, retry and escalation belong entirely to the notification service.

composition.purpose: WM-XCT-036 is registered as a child of the identification model. Reports cite identifier endpoints and asserting authorities as references only; identifier minting, scheme registration, syntax and resolution stay in the parent. Because OWL 2 makes no unique name assumption, the parent's distinct identifiers are neither same nor different by default, which is precisely why the equivalence and reporting surface is added here rather than there.

composition.target: W3C PROV-O provenance and lineage model
composition.purpose: Report-instance provenance and impact lineage are expressed with derivation, revision, attribution and invalidation relations, and generation and invalidation times. The alignment is a vocabulary binding: PROV owns activity, agent and bundle record semantics, and a report instance is never presented as a provenance store or as an audit trail.

composition.target: Records retention, disposition authority and legal hold register model
composition.purpose: Readiness reports carry retention rule references, hold and freeze citations and issuing-authority references. That model owns schedules, disposition authority, hold placement and release, and the execution of destruction, transfer and erasure; NARA practice shows holds are issued and released by an external authority and merely suspend the disposition cycle. This model reports readiness and hands off; it never executes.

Change notice content produced here is handed to a service that owns inbox discovery, delivery, storage, receipt and escalation. Linked Data Notifications deliberately leaves the payload vocabulary open while fixing the sender, receiver and consumer roles, so carrying the payload confers no delivery semantics.

composition.target: Shape and constraint validation service (validation-report producer)
composition.purpose: The conflict report borrows the validation-report shape - focus item, source constraint component, severity, message, detail nesting, and a conformance flag that separates no results from validated as correct - so consumers can read it with existing tooling. Referencing that shape grants no ownership of evaluation, execution or enforcement; the engine and its runtime remain external.

composition.target: Data quality, confidence and assurance measurement model
composition.purpose: Confidence-divergence conflicts and completeness qualifiers cite externally computed quality measurements and externally assigned identity assurance levels by reference. Metric definition and computation stay in the quality model; this model records the citation and never normalises differing scales into one number.

Report issuance, reissue and release events are emitted for recording by the adopting Dimension's audit model. This model neither constructs, seals, stores nor attests an audit trail, and a report instance carries no tamper-evidence guarantee.

composition.target: Subject entity models that adopt the alias mixin
composition.purpose: The reporting surface attaches to any subject model whose records carry alias assertions across authorities, in the way that a patient record carries links to duplicate records of the same individual and a concept carries graded mapping relations to concepts in other schemes. The adopting model keeps its own identity, lifecycle and access rules unchanged.

owner_package_requirements: A named owner accountable for each report series, distinct from the owner of the alias assertions being reported on, so that reporting neutrality is structurally visible.

A declared conflict-class, trigger-class and readiness-status vocabulary with a version identifier bound into every report instance, plus a named steward empowered to add namespaced extensions without redefining base codes.

Declared external executors named by reference before the first report is released: the records authority that executes disposition, the notification service that delivers notices, the authorization service that decides release, and the audit model that records issuance events.

A declared retention rule for the report instances themselves and for the frozen scope bindings and input snapshots they depend on, since a report that outlives its reproducibility basis cannot be verified.
A declared jurisdiction context per adopting Dimension, because disposition authority, hold practice and notification obligations differ by regime.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Local identifiers use the reserved als-report prefix within this model. Report series identifiers are namespaced under the adopting Dimension's registry namespace and must be resolvable to the accountable owner. Vocabulary codes for conflict classes, trigger classes and readiness statuses are namespaced: base codes under the model's own namespace, extensions under a namespace controlled by the adopting Dimension. Referenced identifier endpoints, retention rules, holds and quality measurements always keep the namespace of their owning authority and are never rewritten into a local namespace, since rewriting an identifier is itself an alias assertion and would silently create the equivalence a report is supposed to examine.
registry_links: vr.wm-xct-036 as the registry entry for this model, with nav path NAV.XCT.ALS and domain tag XCT.ALS
WM-XCT-011 as the registered parent identification model
The adopting Dimension's register of report series owners, external executors and jurisdiction contexts

canonicalization_rules: Conflict results are ordered deterministically by conflict class code, then by the sorted participant identifiers, then by the source constraint reference; where a presentational ordering by authority or confidence is also shown it is carried as a separate, labelled view and never as the canonical order.

All time values are normalised to RFC 3339 with explicit seconds and an explicit offset; the originally recorded offset is preserved alongside any UTC normalisation, and -00:00 is retained where it was asserted because it means the local offset is unknown rather than that UTC was preferred.

Identifier endpoints are compared using only the normalisation rules published by their owning authority; no case folding, trimming or scheme rewriting is applied locally, because any such normalisation would itself constitute an unasserted equivalence claim.
Impacted items are grouped by impact surface and then by impacted item reference, so that two runs over the same frozen snapshot produce byte-identical canonical output and can be digest-compared.
patch_rules: Released report instances are append-only and are never edited in place; a correction is a new instance in the same series carrying a revision link to its predecessor and a stated reissue reason.
A predecessor instance is annotated with a superseded marker as a separate, additive annotation; its content is never removed or altered by the reissue.

Retracting a report is itself a new instance that states the retraction and its reason; a retracted instance remains retrievable under its retention rule so that consumers who acted on it can reconstruct what they saw.
The frozen scope binding and input snapshot referenced by an instance are immutable; if inputs change, a new binding is created and a new instance is issued rather than the old binding being updated.
compatibility_rules: Conflict, trigger and readiness vocabularies extend only by adding namespaced codes; consumers must carry unknown codes through unchanged and must not treat an unknown code as absent, as benign, or as equivalent to a known code.
Removing or redefining a base code is a breaking change requiring a new vocabulary major version and a deprecation period during which both versions resolve.

Severity vocabularies are declared per report rather than assumed; a consumer mapping between a three-level and a five-level severity scale must record the mapping used, because no lossless mapping exists between them.

Adding a new impact surface or readiness status is minor only if reports continue to declare which surfaces and statuses were assessed, so that a consumer can distinguish not present from not assessed.

identity_priority: The authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record that owns the object - for a report instance, the identifier assigned by the system that generated and released it; for a referenced alias endpoint, hold, retention rule or quality measurement, the identifier assigned by its own owning authority, which is carried unaltered.
A governed global identifier or IRI from a normative registry or namespace where the object is registered in one, used when no master system owns it.
A UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, used only when neither of the above exists, and recorded as locally minted so consumers can tell it apart from an authoritative identifier.
Never a date, an eligibility date, a generation timestamp, a sequence position, a digest alone, or a file name; these may label or verify an object but they never identify it.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Every time value is an RFC 3339 date-time with explicit seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; -00:00 is used only where UTC is known but the local offset is not, and is preserved rather than rewritten to Z. Event time, observation time and ingestion time are recorded in separate fields and are never collapsed into one: event time is when the reported change actually occurred in its source authority; observation time is when this model observed it, and includes the report's observation cut-off; ingestion time is when the input snapshot was bound. A report instance additionally carries its own generation time and the covered event-time range, which are distinct from all three. Where a source supplies only one time, which one it is must be stated rather than assumed.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Report instances are serial artifacts addressed as series-identifier plus instance-identifier, where the instance identifier is minted under the identity priority above. Sequence position, generation date and any human-readable label such as a quarter or a run number may be carried as descriptive attributes for display and ordering, but never as the identity; two instances generated in the same second must remain distinguishable, and re-running a series must never reuse a retired instance identifier.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every released report instance carries a content digest computed over its canonical form, together with digest-bound references to the frozen scope binding and input snapshot it was produced from. A digest mismatch on the instance or on either dependency invalidates the reproducibility claim: the instance must be reissued as a new instance with a stated reason and must never be repaired in place. Where an instance's input snapshot has been disposed of under its retention rule, the instance is marked as no longer independently reproducible rather than being presented as verified.

policies: Non-adjudication: reports state findings and never resolve them. No report function may mark a participating claim correct or incorrect, alter an assertion's lifecycle state or confidence, or change a derived cluster. Severity and ordering are significance signals for a human or an external decision process, never a ruling, and any accountable adjudicator is named by reference only.

Minority-claim preservation: every claim inside a report's declared scope appears in the report regardless of the weight of its asserting authority or the level of its confidence. Omission is permitted only for a disclosed, scope-based reason, and the disclosed reason must distinguish out of scope, unreachable and later than cut-off from any judgement about merit.

No execution: this model performs no deletion, destruction, transfer or anonymisation; places, extends or releases no hold or freeze; makes no authorization decision; constructs no audit trail; and delivers no notification. Each of these belongs to a referenced model or to the adopting Dimension's policy, named before the first report is released.

Declared incompleteness: a report always states how completely its declared scope was actually examined. Unreachable authorities, unenumerated downstream references and undetermined readiness are reported explicitly. Silence is never a finding: no conflict found is not confirmation of sameness, and unenumerated reach is not absence of impact.

Referenced-not-owned data: retention rules, holds, quality measurements, assurance levels, identifier endpoints and downstream reference indexes are carried by reference with their owning authority's identifier and version. This model never copies, normalises, recomputes or re-keys them.

read: Released report instances are immutable and readable within their per-section access scope, as decided and enforced by the external authorization service; this model records the classification and the decision reference but makes no access decision.
Unreleased draft instances, frozen scope bindings and input snapshots are readable only by the report producer role and the report series owner.
Reading a report instance must also surface its provenance record, its coverage and completeness statement and any superseded marker, so a consumer cannot read findings without reading their limits.
Report content may be read in redacted form for a stated audience scope, with the sections withheld from that audience listed rather than silently absent.
create: A report instance may be created only from a frozen, digest-bound scope binding and input snapshot; ad hoc generation over live sources is refused because it is not reproducible.
Creation must record the generating agent, generation time, observation cut-off, covered event-time range and the vocabulary and rule versions in force.
Creation of a conflict, impact or readiness report never creates, modifies or deletes any alias assertion, derived cluster, hold or retention rule.
A draft instance exists only until release; on release it becomes immutable and acquires its series membership.
update: Released report instances are never mutated. Any change is a new instance in the same series with a revision link and a stated reason.

Only additive annotations may be attached to a released instance: a superseded marker, an access classification, a redaction record, and a not-independently-reproducible marker where its input snapshot has been disposed of.
Vocabulary versions bound into a released instance are never retro-fitted; a report is always read against the vocabulary it was issued under.
Referenced external data - retention rules, holds, assurance levels, quality measurements - is never updated by this model, only re-cited in a later instance.
delete: A released report instance is never hard-deleted by this model. On authorised disposition it is replaced by a tombstone retaining only the instance identifier, the series identifier, the former type of the disposed record, the disposition time, the revision or superseded-by link and the disposition authority reference; all conflict, impact and readiness content is removed so that dangling downstream references resolve to an explanatory marker rather than to nothing.

Retention periods, disposition authority, holds and freezes for these records are owned by the referenced records retention, disposition authority and legal hold register model; execution of destruction, transfer or erasure is performed by that model or by the adopting Dimension's records policy under its own instrument, never by this model. This model produces only the readiness assessment and the handoff payload.

A record classified blocked, retained or not assessed is not eligible for disposition; only the issuing authority may release a hold or freeze, after which readiness must be re-reported before any execution.

Draft, unreleased instances and expired scope bindings may be discarded under the adopting Dimension's operational retention policy without a tombstone, because they were never released and no consumer can have relied on them; the input snapshots they reference follow the snapshot retention rule declared by the series owner.

Where erasure of personal data is required, residue is limited to non-identifying control metadata and a re-identification risk note is recorded. The controller obligation to communicate rectification, erasure or restriction to each recipient - unless that proves impossible or involves disproportionate effort - is discharged by the external notification service using content this model may compose; this model neither judges what constitutes disproportionate effort nor certifies that the obligation has been met.

roles.name: Report series owner
responsibilities: Accountable for a named report series, its scope, its cadence and its declared external executors
Registers the series owner separately from the owner of the alias assertions being reported on, preserving reporting neutrality
Approves release of an instance and the audience scopes it may be redacted for
Declares the retention rule for the series and for its scope bindings and snapshots

roles.name: Report producer
responsibilities: Binds scope and input snapshots and executes the report functions
Records provenance, observation cut-off, covered event-time range and coverage completeness on every instance
Issues corrections as new instances with a stated reason and never edits a released instance
Reports failure modes explicitly rather than releasing a silently degraded report

roles.name: Vocabulary steward
responsibilities: Maintains the conflict-class, trigger-class and readiness-status vocabularies and their versions
Reviews namespaced extensions proposed by the adopting Dimension and refuses redefinition of base codes
Manages deprecation periods so both versions resolve during transition
Publishes the equivalence-strength vocabulary bindings that reports must cite

roles.name: Records and disposition authority liaison
responsibilities: Supplies resolvable retention rule, hold and freeze references and their issuing authorities
Receives the readiness handoff payload and returns confirmation of executed disposition as an external input
Notifies the series owner when a hold is placed or released so readiness statuses can be re-reported
Confirms which model or adopting-Dimension policy executes disposition in each jurisdiction context

roles.name: Report consumer and downstream integrator
responsibilities: Consumes report instances and notice content, and carries unknown vocabulary codes through unchanged
Declares the completeness of any downstream reference index it supplies
Performs its own propagation and reconciliation; this model reports impact but does not update consumer systems
Reports back discrepancies between a report's findings and its own observed state

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Every read of a report bundle, layer, finding or artifact requires an explicit grant evaluated and enforced by the adopting Dimension's external authorization service; this model records the access classification, the redaction applied and the decision reference, and makes no authorization decision itself.
exceptions: A blocked disposition-readiness status and its issuing-authority citation may be exposed to the records authority liaison even where the underlying alias content is restricted, because suppressing the block would risk premature disposal.

Coverage, completeness and residual-uncertainty statements are released with any released report content and may never be withheld while findings are shown, since findings without their limits are misleading.
Where personal data is involved, notice content and tombstone residue are restricted to non-identifying control metadata regardless of the recipient's broader grant.
A superseded marker and the revision link to a successor instance are visible to anyone who could read the predecessor, so that no consumer can act on a retracted or corrected report unknowingly.
Emergency read of a released instance may be granted by the report series owner where a false strong-identity discovery is being investigated, recorded as an exception with its reason and time.
audit_requirements: Report generation, release, reissue, retraction and redacted-release events must be emitted to the adopting Dimension's audit and event-log model, which owns the construction, sealing and retention of the audit trail; this model neither stores nor attests it.

Each emitted event must carry the report instance identifier, series identifier, generating agent, generation time and, for a release, the audience scope and the external authorization decision reference.
Access-exception grants must be emitted with their stated reason and the granting role.

Confirmation of executed disposition received from the records authority must be emitted as a received-input event, distinguishing the time the disposition occurred from the time this model observed the confirmation.
This model relies on the audit model for evidential weight and makes no independent non-repudiation claim about its own records.

required_fields: External executors (records authority, notification service, authorization service, audit model)
read_order: AGENTS.md - identify the model by Name and Type, then resolve Specification URL for the semantics, Storage type URL for the projection in use (including MongoDB or an MCP-exposed store), Interface URL for the access surface and Processes URL for the report operations.

The model specification: read the model scope statement, in-scope and out-of-scope lists and the boundary notes before reading any bundle, so that target-owned concepts are recognised as references rather than as local capability.

The service layers: read the policies (non-adjudication, minority-claim preservation, no execution, declared incompleteness, referenced-not-owned) and the artifact rules for identity, timestamps and integrity before creating or interpreting any report.
The bundles in order: conflict and change-impact reporting, then disposition readiness and report release governance.

The named external executors listed in AGENTS.md: confirm each is resolvable before releasing a report, because a readiness report with no executor and a notice with no delivery service are both incomplete.

coverage.claim: This model covers the conflict, impact and disposition-readiness reporting surface of WM-XCT-036 with structure grounded in primary standards from six independent organizations: report shape and severity grading from SHACL and FHIR OperationOutcome, equivalence semantics and formal contradiction from OWL 2 and SKOS, ordinal cross-system link confidence and directed supersession from FHIR Person and Patient, lineage from PROV-O, disposition phases and hold practice from NARA, downstream notification obligation from Regulation (EU) 2016/679 Article 19, payload-versus-delivery separation from Linked Data Notifications and the Activity Vocabulary, and time semantics from RFC 3339. No single standard covers alias conflict reporting end to end, so the composition of these sources - not any one of them - is the claim, and it is offered as falsifiable rather than complete.

checklist.notes: Report instance and series identity, deterministic conflict-result identity across reissues, and an identity priority whose first entry is the authoritative master-system identifier, with dates, digests and sequence positions explicitly excluded from identifying anything. Identifier endpoints keep their owning authority's namespace.

Report instances move draft to released to superseded or retracted to tombstoned, with append-only reissue. Assertion lifecycle states are read and reported (supersession versus retraction distinguished by retrospective reach) but never changed here; transitions are owned by the assertion surface and its authorities.

Conflict participants with roles and authorities, impact lineage chains, cluster predecessor and successor links with per-member fate, revision links between instances, and eight composition links naming what is referenced rather than owned.

Event, observation and ingestion times are separate fields, plus generation time, observation cut-off and covered event-time range. Interval relations drive time-dependent conflict classes; retrospective windows bound retraction and false-identity impact. RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset throughout, preserving -00:00.

Per-instance provenance record with attribution, frozen scope binding, digest-bound input snapshot and vocabulary versions; PROV-O is an alignment, not an internalisation. Reproducibility is claimed only while the snapshot survives, and is explicitly revoked when it does not.

Five roles, with the report series owner deliberately separated from the owner of the alias assertions being reported on. Every external executor - records authority, notification service, authorization service, audit model - must be named by reference before the first release.

Report structure aligns to the validation-report pattern (focus item, source constraint, severity, conformance flag) so consumers can check findings with existing tooling. Execution of validation and any policy evaluation stays with the external engine; this model owns the report shape, not the evaluator.

Deny by default across bundle, layer, finding and artifact scopes, with per-section classification, audience redaction and five stated exceptions. Authorization decisions are made and enforced externally; this model records the classification and the decision reference only.

Tombstone residue limited to non-identifying control metadata; retention rules, holds and execution owned by the referenced records model or adopting-Dimension policy; drafts discardable without tombstone; readiness statuses blocked, retained, externally governed and not assessed all bar disposition. Readiness is reported, never executed.

Namespaced extensible vocabularies with a carry-unknown-codes rule, declared severity vocabularies with no assumed mapping, declared equivalence-strength bindings per authority, delivery-neutral notice content, and an AGENTS.md bootstrap that names the storage and interface projections.

Non-adjudication and minority-claim preservation are model policies, function effects, a dedicated finding, and canonicalization rules that keep any authority-weighted ordering as a labelled presentational view separate from the canonical order.

Coverage completeness, downstream reach completeness and residual uncertainty are required outputs. The rules that no conflict found is not confirmation of sameness, and that unenumerated reach is not absence of impact, are stated in policy and in function failure modes.

Notice content is produced and redacted here; inbox discovery, delivery, receipt, retry and escalation are external, following the sender/receiver/consumer separation and the deliberately open payload vocabulary of Linked Data Notifications.

Jurisdiction is carried as a first-class parameter and externally governed is a first-class readiness status, but the model supplies no jurisdiction-specific rule content. Verified disposition and hold practice is US federal (NARA) plus one notification obligation from Regulation (EU) 2016/679; other regimes are assumed to differ and are unverified here.

Confidence divergence and reach completeness are cited by reference to externally computed measurements. There is no verified primary standard for quantifying downstream reference reach, so the uncertainty qualifier is a structural placeholder rather than a grounded metric; DQV, the nearest vocabulary, is a non-normative Working Group Note.

Transport security, authentication, signing and non-repudiation are properties of the interface and of the external authorization, notification and audit services. This model deliberately makes no independent non-repudiation claim about its own report instances.

known_omissions: No verified primary standard defines endpoint or cluster split. FHIR Patient.link covers directed supersession (replaced-by, replaces) and non-replacing reference (refer, seealso), but unmerge and split are under-specified in every source consulted; the split representation here, including per-member fate and undetermined assignments, is structurally reasoned rather than standards-derived and is marked a gap.

Quantitative estimation of downstream reference reach for unenumerable consumers - cached copies, offline replicas, unindexed integrations - has no verified standard. The reach completeness qualifier records that the question was asked and answered honestly; it does not make the answer measurable.
What constitutes disproportionate effort under the Article 19 notification obligation is not modelled. No threshold, cost basis or test is supplied, because none is defined in the verified source.

Cryptographic signing, timestamping authority and non-repudiation of report instances are deferred entirely to an external attestation service. The integrity rule uses content digests, which detect corruption but do not establish authorship.
Localisation and translation of conflict messages, status basis notes and notice content are out of scope; only the audience-scope redaction dimension is modelled.

Cost, latency and scale characteristics of producing reports over very large federated assertion sets are not modelled; the frozen-snapshot requirement has real operational cost that this model states as a constraint without sizing.
Human workflow for acting on a report - triage queues, assignment, escalation timers - is deliberately absent, because it belongs to whatever process model consumes the report.
conflicts: SKOS declares exactMatch transitive but deliberately declines to declare closeMatch transitive, precisely to avoid compound errors when chaining mappings across more than two schemes, while OWL 2 SameIndividual is strict identity and PROV-O alternateOf is weaker still. Treating these as one same-as strength produces chains that no source endorses; reports must therefore cite the strength vocabulary and version each participant used, and the model refuses to normalise across them.

FHIR Person.link.assurance is an ordinal four-level scale (level1 probabilistic through level4 highest) with no defined probability semantics, whereas DQV measurements are numeric values of a declared metric. The two cannot be arithmetically combined or ranked against each other, so a confidence-divergence conflict reports both by reference and computes no unified score.

SHACL severity has three levels (Violation, Warning, Info) while FHIR OperationOutcome has five (fatal, error, warning, information, success). There is no lossless mapping in either direction, so severity vocabularies are declared per report rather than assumed, and any consumer-side mapping must be recorded.

Records-management practice suspends disposition indefinitely under a hold until the issuing authority formally releases it, whereas the Article 19 obligation pushes toward prompt communication of erasure or restriction to recipients. These can pull in opposite directions for the same record: this model reports both the block and the notification-content obligation and adjudicates neither, leaving the tension visible to the accountable authorities.

OWL 2 has no unique name assumption, so the absence of a not-same constraint carries no information about difference and the absence of a conflict carries no information about sameness. Any consumer treating a clean conflict report as confirmation of identity is misreading it; this is stated in policy and in the conflict function's failure modes rather than left implicit.
DQV is a W3C Working Group Note whose publication explicitly does not imply W3C endorsement, so alignment to it is non-normative and is recorded as an alignment only, never as conformance.

Patient.link is a modifier element in FHIR, meaning the link type changes how the whole record is interpreted, whereas SKOS mapping properties are additive annotations that change nothing about the concept. A report that mixes both kinds of link must not present them as the same sort of statement.
regional_assumptions: Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 was verified through the legislation.gov.uk rendering of the assimilated text; the EU-official text at EUR-Lex was not reachable during this research, so the source is recorded at authority tier 2 and the quoted obligation should be re-verified against the Official Journal text before any conformance claim.

Disposition and hold practice is verified only for United States federal records through NARA's Universal ERM Requirements and the Federal Records Centers freeze process, which distinguish an agency-issued litigation hold from a NARA freeze over records in Federal Records Center custody. Other jurisdictions place, scope and release holds differently, and the readiness status set is parameterised by jurisdiction for that reason.

FHIR identity assurance levels reflect healthcare identity practice, where level3 is exemplified by government-issued photo identification. They are not a general-purpose confidence scale and should not be reused outside that framing without local calibration.

No single jurisdiction is assumed to govern all endpoints in a federated alias set. Each participating authority may sit under a different regime, which is why externally governed is a first-class readiness status rather than an error condition.
Only English-language primary sources were consulted; national records or identity-matching standards published in other languages may define conflict or disposition classes not represented here.
adversarial_checks: Does any bundle, layer, finding or function let this model resolve a conflict, rank a claim out of existence, delete a record, place or release a hold, decide access or write an audit trail? Every function's effects were re-read against every composition rationale. Result: none does. Severity and ordering are explicitly non-resolutive; deletion, hold placement, authorization and audit construction appear only as REFERENCE links, out_of_scope entries and boundary notes, and each function states them as prohibited effects.

Could a conflict or readiness report be mistaken for an audit record and relied on evidentially? Rejected. Report instances carry provenance and content digests, which support reproducibility but not tamper-evidence. The audit link is a REFERENCE, the model makes no non-repudiation claim, and the security checklist row states this rather than hiding it.

Does impact reporting duplicate the entity-resolution engine's matching semantics? Checked and rejected. The impact function consumes a classified trigger plus prior and posterior state references and never recomputes a match, a score or a blocking key; match computation is an out_of_scope entry and a REFERENCE to the quality and measurement model.

Is a clean conflict report presented anywhere as proof of sameness? Rejected on OWL 2 grounds: no unique name assumption means silence entails nothing. The conformance-style summary is paired with a mandatory coverage statement, unreachable authorities degrade rather than clear a report, and the prohibition is repeated in policy, in the function failure modes and in the recorded conflicts.

Does disposition readiness quietly assume US federal records law? Partly, and it is disclosed. The status set is jurisdiction-parameterised, externally governed is first-class, and the regional assumption records that only NARA practice and one EU-derived notification obligation were verified. Jurisdiction is marked a gap in the checklist rather than presented as covered.

Which attractive structure was proposed and rejected for lack of primary support? A conflict-resolution workflow layer (target-owned: adjudication belongs to a named accountable party, not to a reporting mixin); a notification delivery and subscription layer (target-owned per the sender/receiver/consumer separation in Linked Data Notifications); a tombstone-production finding (would have implied this model performs deletion, so residue is declared as a rule set and the tombstone is created by the executing records authority); and a unified numeric confidence score reconciling assurance levels with quality metrics (no source supports the arithmetic).

Does the reporting surface silently reproduce the parent identification model's identity machinery? Checked against the CHILD relation rationale. This model mints identifiers only for its own report instances and results; every referenced endpoint, hold, retention rule and measurement is carried in its owning authority's namespace, and the canonicalization rules explicitly forbid local identifier rewriting on the grounds that rewriting would itself be an unasserted equivalence claim.
